prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1046; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On a weekday afternoon in Baytown, Texas, Driver 2 was stopped in a traffic lane when the vehicle operated by Driver 1 struck the rear of Driver 2's car. Driver 1 is identified as the named insured on the policy for the vehicle. Passenger was also present in Driver 1's vehicle, and both the responding officer and statements from the scene confirm that Passenger was seated inside at the time of impact. Driver 1 reported neck strain and was evaluated at the scene. The reported injury is consistent with the type and force of a rear-end collision of this kind. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to both vehicles that is largely consistent with the described impact, and they confirm several details given by the drivers. No independent witnesses were located. No prior damage to either vehicle is known to the reporting officer. Both vehicles were driven from the scene after exchanging information, and no citations were issued at the time of this report.
